creative_guardrails.test_market: Malaysia and Philippines via META Android
never_do: Claim features that do not exist in-game
Open with logos, title cards, or slow pans
Use text-heavy intros before gameplay is shown

marketing_angles.name: Hero Showoff
marketing_angles.core_message: Every Eternal plays differently. Find yours.
creative_directions: Fast cuts between hero ultimates and Super Attacks — visual spectacle
Which hero are you? — personality-based hook
One hero per ad showcasing their defining skill
Contrast two heroes with opposite playstyles side by side
messaging_examples: Pick your Eternal. Dominate the arena.
Every Eternal. One arena. Zero excuses.
Master yours.

cps_ir_notes.ThreeSecondPlayRate: High — strong visual variety triggers immediate curiosity
cps_ir_notes.ThruPlayRate: Medium — maintain novelty with hero variety to avoid drop-off

marketing_angles.name: Co-op / Social
marketing_angles.core_message: Better with a partner. More fun with a friend.
creative_directions: Split-screen showing two friends reacting to a clutch win
Play with your duo — couple or best friend framing
Rivals-to-teammates arc: trash talk → coordination → victory
Real people playing together in POV format
messaging_examples: 3 minutes. You and your duo vs. the world.
Your best battles are side by side.
Team up. Take over.

cps_ir_notes.ThruPlayRate: High — social narrative arc naturally builds to a payoff
cps_ir_notes.CTR: Medium-High — social proof and shared emotion drive taps

marketing_angles.name: Ranked Climb
marketing_angles.core_message: You are Bronze now. You will not stay there.

format.style: Narrative arc, rank-up moment as climax

creative_directions: Rank-up moment as climax — rank badge animation with enemy reacting
How far can you climb? — open challenge framing
Losing a close match → learning → winning → rank up arc
Leaderboard reveal with player name climbing to the top
messaging_examples: Bronze today. Immortal is waiting.
Climb the ranks. Prove your skill.
8 tiers. One goal. Get to the top.
Real players. Real ranks. No shortcuts.

cps_ir_notes.ThruPlayRate: High — rank progression arc gives viewers a reason to watch to the end
cps_ir_notes.CTR: High — competitive identity is a strong tap motivator for core gamers

marketing_angles.name: Fast Match / Play Anywhere
marketing_angles.core_message: A full MOBA battle in 3 minutes. No excuses not to play.
target_audiences: Lapsed MOBA players burned out by long sessions

format.style: Situational hook, fast-cut full match, before/after

creative_directions: Full match shown in fast-cut within the ad runtime — real-time countdown visible
Situational micro-moment hook: Waiting for coffee? Play a match.
Side-by-side comparison: Other MOBAs 30 min vs. Blitz of Battle 3 min
End-of-match screen showing match duration as the punchline
messaging_examples: 3-minute MOBA. Full skill. No time wasted.
One match. Three minutes. That's all it takes.
The MOBA that fits your life.
No 30-minute sessions. Just wins.

cps_ir_notes.ThreeSecondPlayRate: High — situational hooks are immediately relatable
cps_ir_notes.CTR: High — time-saving value prop is a clear and compelling tap motivator

marketing_angles.name: Prove Yourself
marketing_angles.core_message: You were doubted, outranked, or losing — and you won anyway.
target_audiences: Casual players intimidated by competitive games
marketing_angles.creative_principle: Struggle is the hook. Victory is the payoff. Do not resolve tension early.
creative_directions: Rank disparity shown on screen — Bronze player beats Gold enemy — rank revealed as punchline
Open on losing state with low health and outnumbered — Super Attack activates — match reversed
Enemy taunting mid-match — gets outplayed immediately after
New player lands their first perfect Super Attack — nobody expected it
Text overlay at turning point: They thought it was over.
messaging_examples: They counted you out. Big mistake.
Rank doesn't win matches. Skill does.
Low health. High stakes. No surrender.
Nobody saw that coming. Especially them.
The best matches start when you're losing.

cps_ir_notes.ThruPlayRate: High — build tension slowly, do not front-load the win
cps_ir_notes.ThreeSecondPlayRate: Medium — open on a clearly losing or underdog state to create immediate stakes

marketing_angles.name: Domination / PvP Flex
marketing_angles.core_message: No struggle needed. You are already the best in the lobby.
target_audiences: Social players who want to flex wins
marketing_angles.creative_principle: No narrative arc. Pure skill gap on display from frame one. Front-load dominance.
creative_directions: Flawless match — enemy eliminated before they can react, zero drama
MVP badge and victory screen close-up → leaderboard showing player at the top
Duo steamrolling — 2v2 where the enemy never stood a chance
Quick-cut montage of 3-4 dominant plays with no explanation
Implicit social flex — Send this to your friends framing
messaging_examples: Some players climb ranks. Others just own them.
MVP. Every. Match.
This is what the top of the lobby looks like.
Go on. You earned the flex.
They never had a chance.

cps_ir_notes.ThreeSecondPlayRate: Very High — most visually dominant gameplay must land in first 3 seconds
cps_ir_notes.CTR: High — superiority framing creates strong ego-driven tap impulse

marketing_angles.name: MOBA Burnout Escape
marketing_angles.core_message: Everything you love about MOBAs. None of what burns you out.
target_audiences: Lapsed MOBA players from Wild Rift or Mobile Legends
creative_directions: Open with familiar MOBA pain points — long loading, 20-min match timer, surrender vote — then cut to Blitz's clean 3-min match
Remember when MOBAs were fun? — nostalgic framing into gameplay reveal
Before/after: exhausted player finishing a 30-min MOBA → same player energized playing Blitz back to back
Minimalist text: 30-minute match. Surrender vote at 15. Or... — cut to Blitz gameplay
messaging_examples: MOBA without the burnout.
Remember when this was fun? It still is.
Everything you loved about MOBAs. In 3 minutes.
The MOBA you actually finish.

cps_ir_notes.ThruPlayRate: High — pain point opening creates strong reason to keep watching for the resolution
cps_ir_notes.CTR: High — speaks to an already-motivated audience with a known frustration

marketing_angles.name: Ragebait / Cringe Provocation
marketing_angles.core_message: You could do better than this. Prove it.
target_audiences: Broad — format works before genre interest is established
emotional_territory: Compulsive I need to fix this
marketing_angles.creative_principle: No resolution before CTA. Unresolved tension drives the download. The viewer's only escape is to install and play.
marketing_angles.retention_flag: Monitor D1 retention closely. Broad audience pull may attract lower-intent users. If D1 drops below baseline add a competitive signal before the CTA to filter for MOBA intent.

format.style: Text overlay heavy, deliberately rough, cheap to produce

sub_formats.name: Deliberately Bad Gameplay
sub_formats.description: Player makes the most obviously wrong decisions possible stacked back to back
examples: Full Super Attack charged → player runs away from the fight
Enemy standing at 1 HP → player uses all abilities and misses every one
Power-up sitting next to player → completely ignored while they lose
Player runs in circles while teammate gets eliminated
sub_formats.structure: Bad decision at 0-3s → gets worse at 3-10s → terrible outcome at 10-14s → CTA at 14-15s

sub_formats.name: Wrong Answer Overlay
sub_formats.reason: Lowest production cost, most proven format in mobile UA — test this first
sub_formats.description: Fake interactive question overlaid on gameplay with obviously wrong answer selected confidently
examples: Enemy at 5HP. What do you do? → Run away selected as correct
Super Attack fully charged mid-fight. Use Super? → Wait for later selected
sub_formats.structure: Question appears at 0-2s → wrong answer selected at 2-8s → painful consequence at 8-13s → CTA at 13-15s

sub_formats.name: Fake Advice Seeking
sub_formats.description: Player makes a catastrophic choice framed as genuinely asking the audience what they should have done
examples: Was this the right move? → worst possible decision plays out
Rate my gameplay 1 to 10 → 15 seconds of painful choices
Did I play this correctly? → player stands idle while match ends
sub_formats.structure: Winnable situation shown at 0-2s → catastrophic decisions at 2-12s → terrible outcome at 12-14s → CTA at 14-15s

cta_variants: This guy needs your help. Download now.
Most players can't get past Bronze. Are you different?
Download Blitz of Battle. Don't play like this.

cps_ir_notes.ThreeSecondPlayRate: Very High — cringe hook is immediate with no slow build
cps_ir_notes.ThruPlayRate: Medium — tension holds attention but lack of resolution may cause some drop-off
cps_ir_notes.CTR: High — frustration and superiority create a strong tap impulse
cps_ir_notes.InstallCount: Monitor — broad reach may lower install intent quality
